How `--baseline` matches health findings: per file and category (`count`, the default) or per function identity (`identity`, strict, and only against a baseline that was saved with `--baseline-mode identity`; such a baseline still reads in count mode).

A finding's identity is its file path plus its function name, so renaming or moving a function that is still in the baseline reports it as new. Re-save the baseline after that kind of refactor. Functions that share a name in one file, and unnamed functions, share one identity and can mask each other.

Defaults to `count` when omitted. Saving without the flag refuses to overwrite a baseline that carries identities; pass `--baseline-mode count` explicitly to downgrade such a baseline on purpose.

global_options.long_help:
Exit with code 1 if a loaded --baseline has entries that match nothing in this run.

Stricter than the default advisory warning: any stale entry fails, not just a quarter of the baseline. Applies in every output format. The verdict reaches a machine consumer as `gate_outcomes["stale-baseline"]`, which is published with or without this flag; the flag decides only whether that entry is `enforced`, and the exit code plus one stderr line. Inert when no baseline is loaded, on runs narrowed to part of the project, which cannot judge a baseline saved with another scope, on `health` and `dupes` in production mode, and under `health --report-only`, which never fails a run; such a run prints why it stood down instead of passing quietly. `fallow audit` always analyzes only changed files, so the gate never fires there.

global_options.help: Exit with code 1 if a loaded baseline has a key that the same file at the base ref does not have
global_options.long_help:
Exit with code 1 if a loaded baseline has a key that the same file at the base ref does not have.

Makes a committed baseline shrink-only. A change that adds a finding and re-saves the baseline in the same commit passes `--baseline` and `--fail-on-stale-baseline`; this gate fails it and lists each new key per category on stderr. A renamed file or a moved line gives a new key, so it counts as growth. The base ref is `--baseline-base`, else the `fallow audit` base: `--changed-since` / `--base`, then `FALLOW_AUDIT_BASE`, then the merge-base with the upstream or the remote default branch. A baseline that the base ref does not have is a new baseline and passes with a note. A base ref that git cannot resolve (for example in a shallow clone) exits 2. Applies to `dead-code`, `architecture`, `dupes`, `health`, `audit` and the bare run, and reaches a machine consumer as `gate_outcomes["baseline-growth"]`.

Off by default, because the parser also rejects valid syntax that is newer than the parser. Applies to `dead-code`, `architecture`, `health`, `audit` and the bare run, in every output format. The `failOnParseError` config key arms the same gate. `health --report-only` never fails a run.

Plain `fallow health` (no gate flag) stays advisory and exits 1 on any finding; for a gate on newly-introduced complexity use `fallow audit --gate new-only`

Save a vital signs snapshot for trend tracking. Defaults to `.fallow/snapshots/{timestamp}.json` if no path is given. A given path must resolve inside the project root, its Git work tree, the CI workspace or a temp directory. Forces file-scores, hotspot, and score computation for complete metrics

Compare current metrics against this snapshot file instead of the newest file in `.fallow/snapshots/`. Use it to restore a baseline from external storage in CI. With --group-by, groups are compared by key when the snapshot holds the same grouping. Implies --trend

Path to coverage data for measured per-function CRAP scores. Accepts an Istanbul coverage map JSON file (coverage-final.json, from `jest --coverage`, `vitest run --coverage`, c8 or nyc), a directory containing coverage-final.json, a raw V8 coverage directory (`NODE_V8_COVERAGE=<dir> node --test`), or a single V8 coverage JSON file. A script that differs from the file on disk and has no source map keeps the estimate. Use --coverage-root when the data was generated in a different environment (CI runner, Docker). Affects CRAP scores only, not --coverage-gaps. Also configurable via FALLOW_COVERAGE env var

Absolute prefix to strip from file paths in coverage data before prepending the project root. Use when coverage was generated in a different environment (CI runner, Docker). Example: if coverage paths start with /home/runner/work/myapp and the project root is ./, pass --coverage-root /home/runner/work/myapp

Saved `fallow mutation --format json` report (for example `.fallow/mutation/last-report.json` or the `-o` file of a run). Adds the mutation score of each complexity finding next to its CRAP score. The score never changes CRAP or the health score. A function whose file changed since the run gets no score. Reads the file only; it runs no test
Threshold for hot-path classification

Fraction of total trace count below which an invoked function is classified as `low_traffic` rather than `active`. Expressed as a decimal (e.g. `0.001` for 0.1%). Omit to use the runtime coverage add-on default (0.001)

Surface local security candidates for downstream agent verification (opt-in).

Ships three complementary surfaces. (2) The data-driven `tainted-sink` catalogue: syntactic sink sites matched against a CWE catalogue (`security_matchers.toml`) spanning categories such as dangerous-html, template-escape-bypass, command-injection, code-injection, dynamic-regex, redos-regex, resource-amplification, dynamic-module-load, sql-injection, ssrf, path-traversal, header-injection, open-redirect, cleartext-transport, electron-unsafe-webpreferences, world-writable-permission, insecure-temp-file, mysql-multiple-statements, mass-assignment, weak-crypto, deprecated-cipher, insecure-randomness, unsafe-buffer-alloc, unsafe-deserialization, prototype-pollution, zip-slip, nosql-injection, ssti, xxe, xpath-injection, and webview-injection. (3) `hardcoded-secret`, an include-required category for provider-prefix literals and high-entropy literals assigned to secret-shaped identifiers. It never runs from raw entropy alone. All findings are candidates for verification, not verified vulnerabilities. This command is the only surface for security findings; they never appear under bare `fallow` or the `audit` gate. Build-config and test files are excluded, and public env prefixes such as `NEXT_PUBLIC_` and `VITE_` are treated as public. commands.long_about:
Audit changed files for dead code, complexity, duplication, and styling.

Purpose-built for reviewing AI-generated code and PR quality gates. Combines dead-code + complexity + duplication + styling scoped to changed files and returns a verdict (pass/warn/fail).

`fallow audit` answers "will CI block this?": it gates (exit 1 on a fail verdict). The `review` alias plus `--brief` answer "where do I look?": the same analysis rendered as a deterministic orientation brief that always exits 0, so a reviewer or agent can read it regardless of the verdict. `--format` is orthogonal to `--brief`. When `--changed-since`/`--base` is unset, the base is the git merge-base against the branch's upstream or the remote default (`origin/HEAD`, `origin/main`, `origin/master`); set `FALLOW_AUDIT_BASE` to pin it. By default, only findings introduced by the changeset affect the verdict; inherited findings are reported with new-vs-inherited attribution and individual JSON findings include `introduced: true/false`. The default gate also reports an unused file or unused export outside the changed files that the base does not report: the change removed its last use, or a config change made it unreachable. Use `--gate all` or `[audit] gate = "all"` to fail on every finding in changed files without running the extra base-snapshot attribution pass.

The global --baseline / --save-baseline flags are rejected on audit. Use --dead-code-baseline, --health-baseline, and --dupes-baseline (or their config equivalents) because each sub-analysis uses a different baseline format.

Apply the audit cache cleanup policy and report every entry.

Runs the same reclaim policy every `fallow audit` run already applies silently: cleanup of orphaned marker files, age-based reclaim under the resolved threshold, and cross-repo reclaim of abandoned entries whose recorded owner root no longer exists. environment_variables.name: FALLOW_CREDENTIAL_STORE
environment_variables.description: Credential store for the key that fallow cloud login writes: auto (default: OS keychain, else ~/.config/fallow/credentials), file (credentials file only) or none (no stored key is read or written).

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_CA_BUNDLE
environment_variables.description: Path to a PEM certificate bundle for Fallow Cloud and provider HTTP calls (replaces the default WebPKI roots).

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_UPDATE_CHECK
environment_variables.description: Set to off/0/false to disable the human-TTY upgrade nudge and its background version check.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_CLAUDE_CODE_HINT
environment_variables.description: Set to off/0/false/no/disabled to suppress the one-line Claude Code plugin hint on stderr. Fallow writes the hint only inside a Claude Code session (CLAUDECODE or CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION), for human output without --quiet, outside CI, and when no Fallow plugin or skill is set up for the project. Default on.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_SUGGESTIONS
environment_variables.description: Set to off/0/false/no/disabled to suppress the next_steps[] array of read-only follow-up commands in JSON output (and the human Next: line). Useful for CI consumers that snapshot-diff raw --format json output. Default on.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_TELEMETRY
environment_variables.description: Opt-in telemetry mode: off, on, or inspect (print the payload to stderr without sending). Telemetry is off by default.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_TELEMETRY_DISABLED
environment_variables.description: Admin/fleet kill switch: truthy values hard-disable telemetry and refuse fallow telemetry enable.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_TELEMETRY_DEBUG
environment_variables.description: Truthy values alias FALLOW_TELEMETRY=inspect.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_AGENT_SOURCE
environment_variables.description: Normalized agent vendor for telemetry classification (e.g. claude_code, codex, cursor). Only read when telemetry is on.

environment_variables.name: DO_NOT_TRACK
environment_variables.description: Honored as a top-precedence telemetry kill switch (consoledonottrack.com convention).

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_BIN
environment_variables.description: Path to the fallow binary that the fallow-mcp server runs. When it is unset, the server runs the `fallow` file next to its own executable, else `fallow` on PATH.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_TIMEOUT_SECS
environment_variables.description: MCP server: per-tool-call CLI subprocess timeout in seconds (default 120). Raise for long runs like production coverage on large dumps.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES
environment_variables.description: MCP server: response cap in bytes for each tool call (default 1000000, highest 16777216). A larger response is refused with FALLOW_MCP_SUBPROCESS_OUTPUT_LIMIT and a narrow list of parameters. The max_output_bytes parameter of a call can only lower this cap.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_DIFF_FILE
environment_variables.description: MCP server: path to a unified diff that scopes all findings by changed line.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_CHANGED_SINCE
environment_variables.description: MCP server: git ref that scopes file discovery for analysis tools.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_MCP_WARM_SESSION
environment_variables.description: MCP server: set to 0, false, off or no to stop typed tool calls from keeping parsed modules in memory between calls (default on).

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_INTEGRATION_SURFACE
environment_variables.description: Telemetry integration_surface override for non-CLI surfaces (mcp/lsp/vscode/napi/programmatic). Set by the MCP server on the CLI it spawns.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_MCP_TOOL
environment_variables.description: Telemetry mcp_tool dimension, validated against the MCP tool-name allowlist. Set by the MCP server alongside FALLOW_INTEGRATION_SURFACE=mcp.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_LSP_REUSE_SESSION
environment_variables.description: Language server: set to 0/false/off/no to load a new project session on each analysis run. By default the server keeps one session per project root between saves and parses only the changed files.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_GATE_REPORT
environment_variables.description: Agent gate script of fallow agent install: path of the full JSON report that the gate writes on a block (default .fallow/gate-report.json). The fallow binary does not read it.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_GATE_OUTPUT
environment_variables.description: Agent gate script of fallow agent install: set to json to print the full JSON report on stderr instead of the compact block message. The fallow binary does not read it.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_GATE_MIN_VERSION
environment_variables.description: Agent gate script of fallow agent install: lowest fallow version that the gate accepts. Set it to the empty string to disable the check. The fallow binary does not read it.

environment_variables.name: FALLOW_GATE_DEBUG
environment_variables.description: Agent gate script of fallow agent install: set to a non-empty value to log each command that the gate skips because it is not a git commit or push. The fallow binary does not read it.

output_formats.name: github-annotations
output_formats.help: GitHub workflow-command annotations. Log-based `::warning` annotations render on fork PRs without a write token, unlike the PR-comment/review formats

output_formats.name: github-summary
output_formats.help: GitHub Actions job-summary markdown, for `fallow ... >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"`. Renders on fork PRs without a write token

issue_types.description: File is not reachable from any entry point
issue_types.label: Unused Files

explanation.name: Unused Files
explanation.summary: File is not reachable from any entry point
explanation.rationale: No code runs the file, but people still read it, search it and update it in refactors. A bug fix in the file has no effect on the running program.
explanation.example: src/old-widget.ts is not imported by any entry point, route, script, or config file.
explanation.how_to_fix: Delete the file if it is genuinely dead. If a framework or a tool loads it implicitly, add the file to `entry`, to `supportEntry` for a file that only tests or tooling load, or to `dynamicallyLoaded` for a file that the code loads at runtime by a computed path.

issue_types.description: Export is never imported
issue_types.label: Unused Exports

explanation.name: Unused Exports
explanation.summary: Export is never imported
explanation.rationale: An export that nothing imports looks like an API that other code depends on, so nobody dares to change or remove it. Code that only this export uses stays in the project with it.
explanation.example: export const formatPrice = ... exists in src/money.ts, but no module imports formatPrice.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the export or make it file-local. If it is public API, import it from an entry point or add an intentional suppression with context. To treat exported Effect schemas as type contracts, set effect.schemaExportsAsTypes: fallow then reports them as unused types.

issue_types.description: Type export is never imported
issue_types.label: Unused Types

explanation.name: Unused Type Exports
explanation.summary: Type export is never imported
explanation.rationale: Type-only exports (interfaces, type aliases, enums used only as types) that are never imported. These do not generate runtime code but add maintenance burden.
explanation.example: export interface LegacyProps is exported, but no module imports the type.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the type export, inline it, or keep it behind an explicit API entry point when consumers rely on it. With effect.schemaExportsAsTypes, this rule also reports unused Effect schema exports.

issue_types.description: Exported signature references a private type
issue_types.label: Private Type Leaks
issue_types.note: Opt-in API hygiene check; the rule defaults to off

explanation.name: Private Type Leaks
explanation.summary: Exported signature references a private type
explanation.rationale: Exported values or types whose public TypeScript signature references a same-file type declaration that is not exported. Consumers cannot name that private type directly, so the backing type should be exported or removed from the public signature.
explanation.example: export function makeUser(): InternalUser exposes InternalUser even though InternalUser is not exported.
explanation.how_to_fix: Export the referenced type, change the public signature to an exported type, or keep the helper private.

issue_types.description: Export marked @deprecated is still referenced
issue_types.label: Deprecated Exports in Use
issue_types.note: Opt-in migration sweep; the rule defaults to off

explanation.name: Deprecated Exports in Use
explanation.summary: Export marked @deprecated is still referenced
explanation.rationale: Exports whose leading JSDoc carries @deprecated and that still have at least one consumer in a reachable file. Each finding lists the exact consumer count, a sample of up to 10 consumers sorted by path and line, and the deprecation message. A deprecated export with no consumer is reported as an unused export instead, marked deprecated. A consumer in an unreachable file does not count, because that file is dead code itself. `public_api` is true when the export lives in an entry point or a re-export chain reaches one: external consumers are not visible, so the finding makes no removal claim. The rule is opt-in and defaults to off. A per-path override resolves on the file that declares the export, not on the consumer.
explanation.example: /** @deprecated Use formatMoney. */ export function formatPrice() is still imported by src/cart.ts and src/checkout.ts.
explanation.how_to_fix: Move each consumer to the replacement the message names, then remove the export. For the full consumer list, run `fallow dead-code --trace <file>:<export>`. Enable the rule with `deprecated-exports-in-use: "warn"` in `rules`, or pass `--deprecated-exports-in-use` for one run.

issue_types.description: Dependency listed but never imported
issue_types.label: Unused Dependencies
issue_types.note: --unused-deps controls unused-dependency, unused-dev-dependency, unused-optional-dependency, type-only-dependency, test-only-dependency, and dev-dependency-in-production

explanation.name: Unused Dependencies
explanation.summary: Dependency listed but never imported
explanation.rationale: Packages listed in dependencies that are never imported or required by any source file. A package that only a framework or a CLI tool loads can be reported when no plugin of fallow knows that use. To keep such a package, add it to `ignoreDependencies`.
explanation.example: package.json lists left-pad, but no source, script, config, or plugin-recognized file imports it.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the dependency after checking runtime/plugin usage. If another workspace uses it, move the dependency to that workspace.

issue_types.description: Dev dependency listed but never imported
issue_types.label: Unused Dev Dependencies
issue_types.note: --unused-deps controls unused-dependency, unused-dev-dependency, unused-optional-dependency, type-only-dependency, test-only-dependency, and dev-dependency-in-production

explanation.name: Unused Dev Dependencies
explanation.summary: Dev dependency listed but never imported
explanation.rationale: Every install on every developer machine and in every CI run downloads the package. Its security advisories and version updates still need a review, for a package that no code uses.
explanation.example: package.json lists left-pad, but no source, script, config, or plugin-recognized file imports it.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the dependency after checking runtime/plugin usage. If another workspace uses it, move the dependency to that workspace.

issue_types.description: Optional dependency listed but never imported
issue_types.label: Unused Optional Dependencies
issue_types.note: --unused-deps controls unused-dependency, unused-dev-dependency, unused-optional-dependency, type-only-dependency, test-only-dependency, and dev-dependency-in-production

explanation.name: Unused Optional Dependencies
explanation.summary: Optional dependency listed but never imported
explanation.rationale: The package manager still tries to install the package on each install. Its advisories and version updates still need a review, and readers assume that some platform needs it.
explanation.example: package.json lists left-pad, but no source, script, config, or plugin-recognized file imports it.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the dependency after checking runtime/plugin usage. If another workspace uses it, move the dependency to that workspace.

issue_types.description: Production dependency only used via type-only imports
issue_types.label: Type-Only Dependencies
issue_types.note: Only reported in --production mode; --unused-deps scopes it together with the other dependency kinds

explanation.name: Type-only Dependencies
explanation.summary: Production dependency only used via type-only imports
explanation.rationale: Production dependencies that are only imported via `import type` statements. These can be moved to devDependencies since they generate no runtime code and are stripped during compilation.
explanation.example: zod is in dependencies but only appears in import type declarations.
explanation.how_to_fix: Move the package to devDependencies unless runtime code imports it as a value.

issue_types.description: Production dependency only imported by test files
issue_types.label: Test-Only Dependencies
issue_types.note: Not reported in --production mode (test files are excluded there); --unused-deps scopes it together with the other dependency kinds

explanation.name: Test-only Dependencies
explanation.summary: Production dependency only imported by test files
explanation.rationale: Production dependencies that are only imported from test files. These can usually move to devDependencies because production entry points do not require them at runtime.
explanation.example: vitest is listed in dependencies, but only test files import it.
explanation.how_to_fix: Move the package to devDependencies unless production code imports it at runtime.

issue_types.description: devDependency imported by production code with a runtime import
issue_types.label: Dev Dependencies Used in Production

explanation.name: Dev Dependencies Used in Production
explanation.summary: devDependency imported by production code with a runtime import
explanation.rationale: A package in `devDependencies` that is imported by production (non-test, non-config) source code via a runtime/value import. Whether it should be promoted to `dependencies` depends on the deployment: a production-only install (`pnpm install --prod`) omits devDependencies, so an import resolved at runtime breaks, while a build that inlines the package into its output resolves nothing at runtime and promoting it can instead make the deployment require an install it did not need. This is the promote-side mirror of `test-only-dependency` and `type-only-dependency`. A dev dependency imported from production code only via `import type` is not flagged (types are erased at build time), and a package also listed in `dependencies`, `peerDependencies`, or `optionalDependencies` is left alone because another manifest section provides it at runtime.
explanation.example: yaml is in devDependencies, but src/config.ts imports { parse } from 'yaml' and runs it at runtime.
explanation.how_to_fix: Move the package to dependencies when the deployment installs them, so a production-only install keeps it. Leave it in devDependencies if the build inlines it into the output, if the only production imports are `import type`, or if another manifest section (dependencies / peer / optional) already provides it.

issue_types.description: Enum member is never referenced
issue_types.label: Unused Enum Members

explanation.name: Unused Enum Members
explanation.summary: Enum member is never referenced
explanation.rationale: Readers treat each enum member as a state that can occur, so switch statements, mappings and tests keep a branch for a value that no code uses.
explanation.example: Status.Legacy remains in an exported enum, but no code reads that member.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the member after checking serialized/API compatibility, or suppress it with a reason when external data still uses it.

issue_types.description: Class member is never referenced
issue_types.label: Unused Class Members

explanation.name: Unused Class Members
explanation.summary: Class member is never referenced
explanation.rationale: No code calls the member, but it stays in the public shape of the class. People keep it in step during refactors, and readers assume that some caller depends on it.
explanation.example: class Parser has a public parseLegacy method that is never called in the project.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove or privatize the member. For reflection/framework lifecycle hooks, configure or suppress the intentional entry point.

issue_types.description: Store member is never accessed by any consumer
issue_types.label: Unused Store Members

explanation.name: Unused Store Members
explanation.summary: Store member is never accessed by any consumer
explanation.rationale: Pinia store members (a `state` / `getters` / `actions` key, or a setup-store returned key) declared but never accessed by any consumer project-wide. The store binding is imported (so the module is reachable) yet a specific member is dead. Defaults to warn, not error: a store has an open declaration surface (plugins, dynamic dispatch) so confidence is lower. Activates only when pinia or @pinia/nuxt is a declared dependency.
explanation.example: useCartStore declares a discountTotal getter that no component, composable, or other store ever reads.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the unused state property, getter, or action. If it is consumed reflectively (a Pinia plugin, $onAction, or dynamic dispatch), suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line unused-store-member.

issue_types.description: Protected class member is never referenced
issue_types.label: Unused Protected Class Members

explanation.name: Unused Protected Class Members
explanation.summary: Protected class member is never referenced
explanation.rationale: Class methods and properties with the `protected` modifier that neither the class nor a subclass reads. A read through `this` or `super` in the class or in a subclass counts as a use. A subclass override counts as used when the base class calls the member. Classes of the public API of a package are not checked, because a consumer can subclass them. Production mode ignores reads in test files. Defaults to off. Known limits: a read through a string key (`this["member"]()`) gives no credit, and a constructor parameter property (`constructor(protected readonly x: X)`) is not checked.
explanation.example: class Shape declares protected unusedHelper(), and neither Shape nor a subclass calls this.unusedHelper() or super.unusedHelper().
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the member, or make it private when only the class reads it. If a subclass outside the project reads it, suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line unused-protected-class-member.

issue_types.description: Namespace member is never referenced
issue_types.label: Unused Namespace Members

explanation.name: Unused Namespace Members
explanation.summary: Namespace member is never referenced
explanation.rationale: No code reads the member, but its export makes it look like an API that other code depends on. People keep it in step during refactors and do not dare to remove it.
explanation.example: src/lib/legacy.ts exports namespace Legacy with a member unusedInner that no file reads as Legacy.unusedInner.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the unused member, or remove its export keyword when only the namespace body uses it. For generated code, turn the rule off for those files in overrides. Suppress an intentional member with // fallow-ignore-next-line unused-namespace-member.

issue_types.description: Import could not be resolved
issue_types.label: Unresolved Imports

explanation.name: Unresolved Imports
explanation.summary: Import could not be resolved
explanation.rationale: When the runtime or the bundler cannot resolve the path either, the build fails or the module throws when it loads. fallow also loses the edge, so the files behind it can show up as unused.
explanation.example: src/app.ts imports ./routes/admin, but no matching file exists after extension and index resolution.
explanation.how_to_fix: Fix the specifier, restore the missing file, install the package, or align tsconfig path aliases with the runtime resolver.

issue_types.description: Dependency used but not in package.json
issue_types.label: Unlisted Dependencies

explanation.name: Unlisted Dependencies
explanation.summary: Dependency used but not in package.json
explanation.rationale: Packages imported without an applicable dependency declaration in package.json. This includes workspace packages imported from the repository root: npm workspace links make a package resolvable, but do not declare a dependency. Package self-references are allowed. Private packages and tooling may use ancestor declarations; publishable runtime code must declare its own dependencies.
explanation.example: Root src/app.ts imports @acme/shared, an npm workspace package. The root package.json lists workspaces but does not list @acme/shared as a dependency, so the import is unlisted even when npm links it into node_modules.
explanation.how_to_fix: Declare the imported package in the owning package.json, including the root manifest for root code. Use dependencies for runtime needs or devDependencies for tooling/tests, with a version accepted by your package manager. Self-references need no declaration. For deliberately ambient packages, use ignoreDependencies as an explicit opt-out.

issue_types.description: Binary used but provided by no installed package
issue_types.label: Unlisted Binaries
issue_types.note: Needs installed dependencies; a project without a root node_modules reports none

explanation.name: Unlisted Binaries
explanation.summary: Binary used but provided by no installed package
explanation.rationale: Binaries that package.json scripts or process calls in source (`spawn`, `execSync`, `execa`, the `$` template of zx or execa, `Bun.spawn`) run with a literal command, when no installed or listed package provides them. A binary counts as provided when a `node_modules/.bin` link exists, a declared dependency or a workspace package declares it in `bin`, or it maps to a declared dependency. Shell builtins, commands that `npx` or `pnpm dlx` download, and a fixed list of common operating-system tools are skipped. The check needs installed dependencies and reports nothing without a root `node_modules`. Defaults to warn.
explanation.example: The package.json script `pack` runs `gnome-extensions pack ext`, and src/capture.ts calls `spawnSync("hyprctl", ["version"])`. No installed package provides either binary.
explanation.how_to_fix: Add the package that provides the binary to devDependencies. When the operating system or the CI image provides it, add the name to ignoreBinaries.

issue_types.description: Export name appears in multiple modules
issue_types.label: Duplicate Exports
issue_types.note: fallow fix can add an ignoreExports rule to the fallow config instead of editing source

explanation.name: Duplicate Exports
explanation.summary: Export name appears in multiple modules
explanation.rationale: The same export name is defined in multiple modules. Consumers may import from the wrong module, leading to subtle bugs. Consider renaming or consolidating.
explanation.example: Button is exported from both src/ui/button.ts and src/components/button.ts.
explanation.how_to_fix: Rename or consolidate the exports so consumers have one intentional import target.

issue_types.description: One module exports one binding under two or more names
issue_types.label: Duplicate Export Aliases

explanation.name: Duplicate Export Aliases
explanation.summary: One module exports one binding under two or more names
explanation.rationale: One module exports the same binding under two or more names, for example `export const layer = make(); export default layer;` or `export { a, a as b }`. Consumers can import one value under several names, so the export surface is larger than it needs to be. Fallow groups the exports of a file by binding: a local binding name, or the source and imported name of a named re-export. Value and type-only exports are separate groups, and a plain specifier of a name that the file declares only as a type joins the type group. Two bindings with the same initializer are two bindings and are not reported. `export *`, files with CommonJS exports (`export =`, `module.exports`), component files and unreachable files are skipped. `ignoreExports` exempts a file with `*`, or a binding when one of its names is listed. Default warn. The rule differs from `duplicate-export`, which reports one export name in several files.
explanation.example: src/worker.ts has export const handler = createHandler() and export default handler, so one binding has the names handler and default.
explanation.how_to_fix: Keep one export name and update the importers of the other names. If the names are an intentional public API, add them to ignoreExports, or suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line duplicate-export-alias.

issue_types.description: Circular dependency chain detected
issue_types.label: Circular Dependencies

explanation.name: Circular Dependencies
explanation.summary: Circular dependency chain detected
explanation.rationale: A cycle in the module import graph. Circular dependencies cause undefined behavior with CommonJS (partial modules) and initialization ordering issues with ESM. Break cycles by extracting shared code.
explanation.example: src/a.ts imports src/b.ts, and src/b.ts imports src/a.ts.
explanation.how_to_fix: Extract shared code to a third module, invert the dependency, or split initialization-time side effects from type-only contracts.

issue_types.description: Two or more barrel files re-export from each other in a loop
issue_types.label: Re-Export Cycles

explanation.name: Re-Export Cycles
explanation.summary: Two or more barrel files re-export from each other in a loop
explanation.rationale: A barrel file re-exports from another barrel that ultimately re-exports back. When this happens, imports from any file in the loop may silently come up empty, because the re-export chain has no terminating module to resolve names against. To fix this: open any one file in the loop and remove the `export * from` (or `export { ... } from`) statement that points back into the cycle. Any single removal will break the cycle and restore working re-exports. A self-loop (a single barrel re-exporting from itself, often a rename leftover) is reported under the same rule with kind `self-loop`.
explanation.example: src/ui/index.ts has `export * from './forms'`, and src/ui/forms/index.ts has `export * from '..'`, so the two barrels re-export from each other.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove one `export ... from` statement in the loop that points back into the cycle. For a self-loop, remove the statement with which the file re-exports itself.

issue_types.description: Two or more workspace packages import each other in a loop
issue_types.label: Package Cycles
issue_types.note: Requires a workspace with two or more packages

explanation.name: Package Cycles
explanation.summary: Two or more workspace packages import each other in a loop
explanation.rationale: Workspace packages whose resolved imports form a cycle. Each workspace package is a node and each resolved import from one package to another is an edge, so a package cycle can exist when no file-level cycle exists. Imports from test, spec, story, fixture and tooling config files are not edges, because those files are not part of the package build. Packages in a cycle cannot be built in dependency order. Each hop shows one example import and a `type_only` flag; a type-only hop still matters for declaration builds. To fix this, remove the imports on one hop, for example by moving the shared code to a package that both packages import.
explanation.example: packages/api imports `@acme/db`, and packages/db imports a type from `@acme/api`.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the imports on one hop. Move the code that both packages need into a third package that both packages import.

issue_types.description: Import crosses a configured architecture boundary
issue_types.label: Boundary Violations
issue_types.note: Requires configured boundary zones (boundaries config)

explanation.name: Boundary Violations
explanation.summary: Import crosses a configured architecture boundary
explanation.rationale: A module imports from a zone that its configured boundary rules do not allow. Boundary checks help keep layered architecture, feature slices, and package ownership rules enforceable.
explanation.example: features/billing imports app/admin even though the configured boundary only allows imports from shared and entities.
explanation.how_to_fix: Move the shared contract to an allowed zone, invert the dependency, or update the boundary config only if the architecture rule was wrong.

issue_types.description: Source file matches no configured architecture boundary zone
issue_types.label: Boundary Coverage
issue_types.note: Requires boundaries.coverage.requireAllFiles

explanation.name: Boundary Coverage
explanation.summary: Source file matches no configured architecture boundary zone
explanation.rationale: A file outside every zone is outside every boundary rule, so it can import from any layer. New code in that file can break the architecture, and no check reports it.
explanation.example: src/generated/client.ts is reachable but does not match any boundaries.zones[].patterns entry.
explanation.how_to_fix: Add the file to the intended zone pattern, move it under a zoned directory, or add a generated-file glob to boundaries.coverage.allowUnmatched.

issue_types.description: Zoned file calls a callee its zone forbids
issue_types.label: Boundary Call Violations
issue_types.note: Requires boundaries.calls.forbidden patterns

explanation.name: Boundary Call Violation
explanation.summary: Zoned file calls a callee its zone forbids
explanation.rationale: The zone now performs an effect that the architecture keeps out of it, such as a shell command in domain code. Its tests then need that effect, and reviewers of the zone do not expect it.
explanation.example: src/domain/policy.ts calls execSync from node:child_process while boundaries.calls.forbidden bans child_process.* from the domain zone.
explanation.how_to_fix: Move the call into a zone that may perform the effect, route it through an allowed abstraction, or narrow the forbidden pattern if the rule was wrong. To suppress, use the boundary family token: `// fallow-ignore-next-line boundary-violation` governs import, coverage, and call findings alike (the rule-id-shaped `boundary-call-violation` is accepted as an alias).

issue_types.description: Usage violates a configured rule-pack policy
issue_types.label: Policy Violations
issue_types.note: Requires a configured rule pack (rulePacks config)

explanation.name: Policy Violation
explanation.summary: Usage violates a configured rule-pack policy
explanation.rationale: A call, import, export, catalogue-derived effect, or graph-resolved GDP proof producer violates a configured rule pack (the rulePacks config key). Packs are pure declarative data. Call rules match calls and new expressions, on written plus import-resolved canonical callees. Effect rules match calls only. Import rules match the raw specifier. GDP rules trace @gdp-ts/core proof producers through unambiguous re-exports and restrict which files may create proof factories, optionally by exact static proof kind. This is syntactic ownership analysis, not a runtime authorization guarantee. Follow the rule's message, move a producer into an allowed file, scope the rule with files/exclude globs, or adjust its severity.
explanation.example: src/app.ts imports moment while a rule pack bans the moment specifier with the message 'Use date-fns.'
explanation.how_to_fix: Follow the rule's message to replace banned usage or remove a banned export. For a GDP proof producer, move proof factory creation into an allowed file, or correct the rule's allowedFiles and optional proofKinds if the ownership policy was wrong. For a banned-import rule with allowNames, import a listed name by name. To waive one rule, use `// fallow-ignore-next-line policy-violation:<pack>/<rule-id>` or the file-level form. Use bare `policy-violation` only when you intend to suppress every rule-pack finding at that scope.

issue_types.description: Suppression comment or tag no longer matches any issue
issue_types.label: Stale Suppressions
issue_types.note: Fix by removing the stale suppression marker itself

explanation.name: Stale Suppressions
explanation.summary: Suppression comment or tag no longer matches any issue
explanation.rationale: The comment tells readers that a problem exists where none does. When a new issue of the same kind appears on that line, the old comment hides it from review.
explanation.example: `// fallow-ignore-next-line unused-export` stays above an export that another module imports, so no unused-export finding remains for the comment to suppress.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the suppression. If a different issue is still intentional, replace it with a current, specific suppression.

issue_types.description: Suppression comment omits a required reason
issue_types.label: Missing Suppression Reasons

explanation.name: Missing Suppression Reason
explanation.summary: Suppression comment omits a required reason
explanation.rationale: Without a reason, a reviewer cannot tell if the suppression is a decision or a shortcut. Later, nobody can check if the reason still holds, so the suppression stays forever.
explanation.example: `// fallow-ignore-next-line unused-export` appears without a reason after the token, while `requireSuppressionReason` is on.
explanation.how_to_fix: Add a concise reason after the suppression token, or remove the suppression if the issue is no longer intentional.

issue_types.description: Catalog entry not referenced by any workspace package
issue_types.label: Unused Catalog Entries

explanation.name: Unused catalog entry
explanation.summary: Catalog entry not referenced by any workspace package
explanation.rationale: No package uses the pinned version, but the entry still gets version updates and reviews. Readers assume that some workspace depends on it.
explanation.example: The catalog source declares `catalog: { is-even: ^1.0.0 }`, but no workspace package.json declares `"is-even": "catalog:"`.
explanation.how_to_fix: Delete the entry from the catalog source file. If any consumer uses a hardcoded version (surfaced in `hardcoded_consumers`), switch that consumer to `catalog:` first to keep versions aligned.

issue_types.description: Named catalog group has no entries
issue_types.label: Empty Catalog Groups

explanation.name: Empty catalog group
explanation.summary: Named catalog group has no entries
explanation.rationale: A named group under `catalogs:` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or Bun root `package.json` has no package entries. Empty named groups are leftover catalog structure after the last entry is removed. The default `catalog` map is intentionally ignored because some projects keep it as a stable hook.
explanation.example: The catalog source declares `catalogs: { react17: {} }` after the last react17 entry was removed.
explanation.how_to_fix: Delete the empty named group from the catalog source file. Comments between the deleted header and the next sibling can stay in place for manual review.

issue_types.description: package.json references a catalog that does not declare the package
issue_types.label: Unresolved Catalog References

explanation.name: Unresolved catalog reference
explanation.summary: package.json references a catalog that does not declare the package
explanation.rationale: A workspace package.json declares a dependency with the `catalog:` or `catalog:<name>` protocol, but the catalog has no entry for that package. The package manager install will fail until the catalog is fixed. To fix: add the package to the named catalog, switch the reference to a different catalog that does declare it, or remove the reference and pin a hardcoded version. Scope: the detector scans `dependencies`, `devDependencies`, `peerDependencies`, and `optionalDependencies` in every workspace `package.json`, plus the pnpm override values in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `overrides` (skipped when `packageManager` names a pnpm version that ignores it: pnpm before 10.5.1, or pnpm 10 or earlier when the root `package.json` declares non-empty `pnpm.overrides` or `resolutions`), root `package.json` `pnpm.overrides` (skipped when `packageManager` names pnpm 11 or later, because pnpm 11 does not read it), and root `package.json` `resolutions` (read only when `packageManager` names pnpm 10 or earlier), using `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalogs when present and Bun root `package.json` catalogs otherwise. See also: fallow/unused-catalog-entry (the inverse: catalog entries no consumer references).
explanation.example: packages/app/package.json declares `"old-react": "catalog:react17"`, but `catalogs.react17` in the catalog source does not declare `old-react`. The package manager install will fail.
explanation.how_to_fix: If `available_in_catalogs` is non-empty, change the reference to one of those catalogs (e.g. `catalog:react18`). Otherwise add the package to the named catalog in the catalog source, or remove the catalog reference and pin a hardcoded version. For staged migrations where the catalog edit lands separately, add the (package, catalog, consumer) triple to `ignoreCatalogReferences` in your fallow config.

issue_types.description: Package-manager override target is not declared or resolved
issue_types.label: Unused Dependency Overrides

explanation.name: Unused dependency override
explanation.summary: Package-manager override target is not declared or resolved
explanation.rationale: An entry in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s `overrides:` section (skipped when `packageManager` names a pnpm version that ignores it: pnpm before 10.5.1, or pnpm 10 or earlier when the root `package.json` declares non-empty `pnpm.overrides` or `resolutions`), `package.json#pnpm.overrides` (skipped when `packageManager` names pnpm 11 or later, which does not read it), npm or Bun's top-level `package.json#overrides`, or Bun's `package.json#resolutions` whose target package is not declared by any workspace package and is not present in the active readable lockfile (`pnpm-lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, or `bun.lock`). Override entries linger after their target package leaves the resolved dependency tree. pnpm and npm projects without a readable lockfile fall back to workspace package manifests and keep a `hint` so transitive CVE pins can be reviewed before removal. Bun projects with only binary `bun.lockb` fail closed: fallow reports a workspace diagnostic and emits no unused-override finding until a readable `bun.lock` exists. To fix: delete the entry, refresh the active lockfile if it is stale, or add the entry to `ignoreDependencyOverrides` when the override is intentionally retained. See also: fallow/misconfigured-dependency-override.
explanation.example: The root package.json declares `overrides: { axios: ^1.6.0 }`, but no workspace package.json declares `axios` and the active lockfile does not resolve it.
explanation.how_to_fix: Delete the entry from its reported declaration source. If the finding is caused by a stale or missing readable lockfile, refresh the active lockfile and rerun fallow. If the override is intentionally retained, add it to `ignoreDependencyOverrides` in your fallow config.

issue_types.description: Package-manager override has an unparsable key or value
issue_types.label: Misconfigured Dependency Overrides

explanation.name: Misconfigured dependency override
explanation.summary: Package-manager override has an unparsable key or value
explanation.rationale: An entry in `pnpm-workspace.yaml#overrides` (skipped when `packageManager` names a pnpm version that ignores it: pnpm before 10.5.1, or pnpm 10 or earlier when the root `package.json` declares non-empty `pnpm.overrides` or `resolutions`), `package.json#pnpm.overrides` (skipped when `packageManager` names pnpm 11 or later, which does not read it), npm or Bun's top-level `package.json#overrides`, or Bun's `package.json#resolutions` whose key or value cannot be interpreted in that source's override grammar. Common shapes include an empty key, an empty value, a malformed version selector (`@types/react@<<18`), or an unbalanced parent matcher (`react>`). The active package manager may reject or ignore the entry. To fix: correct the key or value according to that package manager's grammar, or remove the entry. See also: fallow/unused-dependency-override.
explanation.example: The root package.json declares `overrides: { "axios": "" }`. An empty override value is invalid and the active package manager will reject or ignore it.
explanation.how_to_fix: Fix the key or value to match the active package manager's grammar. For pnpm this includes bare or scoped package names, version selectors, parent matchers, and the supported `-`, `$ref`, and `npm:alias` values. For npm or Bun, preserve the supported nested object shape. Remove experimental entries that should not remain.

issue_types.description: "use client" file exports a server-only / route-config name
issue_types.label: Invalid Client Exports
issue_types.note: Requires the project to declare next

explanation.name: Invalid client export
explanation.summary: "use client" file exports a server-only / route-config name
explanation.rationale: Next.js rejects the file when it compiles the route, so the page fails to build. The check reports the export before anyone opens the page or runs the build.
explanation.example: app/page.tsx starts with `"use client"` and exports `metadata`.
explanation.how_to_fix: Move the server-only export to a module without `"use client"`, such as a server component or `layout.tsx`. Or remove the directive when the module does not need to be a client boundary.

issue_types.description: Barrel re-exports both a "use client" module and a server-only module
issue_types.label: Mixed Client/Server Barrels
issue_types.note: Requires the project to declare a React Server Components bundler, such as next, waku or @vitejs/plugin-rsc

explanation.name: Mixed client/server barrel
explanation.summary: Barrel re-exports both a "use client" module and a server-only module
explanation.rationale: A barrel file (a module whose exports are `export ... from` re-exports) forwards a name from a `"use client"` module alongside a name from a server-only module (one carrying `"use server"`, importing the `server-only` package, or importing a server-only Next.js API such as `next/headers`). Importing one name from such a barrel drags the other's directive context across the React Server Components boundary, a known Next.js App Router problem. Type-only re-exports are ignored (erased at build), and a barrel re-exporting a client module alongside an ordinary undirected utility is not reported. To fix: split the barrel so client and server-only modules are re-exported from separate entry points. The check runs only when the project declares a React Server Components bundler: `next`, `waku`, `@lazarv/react-server`, `react-server-dom-webpack`, `react-server-dom-vite`, `react-server-dom-parcel` or `@vitejs/plugin-rsc`.
explanation.example: components/index.ts re-exports `Button` from a `"use client"` module and `getUser` from a module that imports `server-only`.
explanation.how_to_fix: Split the barrel: re-export the client modules from one file and the server-only modules from another file.

issue_types.description: "use client" / "use server" directive is not in the leading position and is ignored
issue_types.label: Misplaced Directives
issue_types.note: Requires the project to declare a React Server Components bundler, such as next, waku or @vitejs/plugin-rsc

explanation.name: Misplaced directive
explanation.summary: "use client" / "use server" directive is not in the leading position and is ignored
explanation.rationale: A `"use client"` or `"use server"` directive string appears as an expression statement after a non-directive statement (an `import`, a `const`). React Server Components bundlers only honor a directive in the leading prologue, before any other statement; once any statement precedes it the string is parsed as an ordinary expression and silently ignored. The intended client/server boundary never takes effect, so the file is treated as a server module. To fix: move the directive to the very top of the file, above every import. The check runs only when the project declares a React Server Components bundler: `next`, `waku`, `@lazarv/react-server`, `react-server-dom-webpack`, `react-server-dom-vite`, `react-server-dom-parcel` or `@vitejs/plugin-rsc`.
explanation.example: A file has `import { useState } from 'react';` on line 1 and `"use client";` on line 2.
explanation.how_to_fix: Move the directive to the first line of the file, above every import.

issue_types.description: inject() / getContext() reads a key that no provide() / setContext() supplies
issue_types.label: Unprovided Injects

explanation.name: Unprovided injects
explanation.summary: inject() / getContext() reads a key that no provide() / setContext() supplies
explanation.rationale: A Vue `inject(KEY)` or Svelte `getContext(KEY)` reads a dependency-injection key (an imported or module-local symbol) that no matching `provide(KEY)` / `setContext(KEY)` supplies anywhere in the project. The read resolves to undefined at runtime, surfaced only at render. To fix: add a matching provider for the key, or remove the dead inject. Defaults to warn, not error: a provider may live outside the analyzed graph (an app-level provide registered elsewhere, a plugin, a host application). String-literal keys and keys imported from a package are abstained.
explanation.example: A component calls inject(ThemeKey) (Vue) or getContext(ThemeKey) (Svelte) with an imported symbol key, but no provide(ThemeKey) / setContext(ThemeKey) exists anywhere in the project.
explanation.how_to_fix: Add a matching provide() / setContext() for the key, or remove the dead inject() / getContext(). If a provider lives outside the analyzed graph (an app-level provide registered elsewhere, a plugin, a host app), suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line unprovided-inject.

issue_types.description: A component is reachable through a barrel but rendered nowhere
issue_types.label: Unrendered Components

explanation.name: Unrendered components
explanation.summary: A Vue / Svelte component is reachable through a barrel but rendered nowhere
explanation.rationale: A component is reachable in the module graph (a barrel re-exports it) but rendered nowhere in the project. The rule covers Vue, Svelte and Astro single-file components (the default export of a `.vue`, `.svelte` or `.astro` file), Angular components with an element selector, and Lit elements. For a single-file component: no `<Tag>`, no `:is` / `this=` binding, no `components` / `app.component` registration, no `h()` / auto-import use, and no script value-read. It survives unused-file (the barrel keeps it reachable) and unused-export (the re-export counts as a use), yet no file actually renders it. To fix: render the component somewhere, or delete it and drop the dead re-export. Defaults to warn, not error: a component can be rendered reflectively (a dynamic `<component :is>` resolved from a non-literal value), so analyzer confidence is lower. Components that are themselves entry points (route pages, layouts, `App.vue`) and components re-exported from a non-private package entry point are abstained.
explanation.example: components/Orphan.vue is re-exported from a barrel (export { default as Orphan } from './Orphan.vue') but no template, registration, h() call, or dynamic import ever renders it.
explanation.how_to_fix: Render the component where it belongs, or delete it and remove the dead barrel re-export. If it is rendered reflectively (a dynamic <component :is> from a non-literal value), suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line unrendered-component.

issue_types.description: Known reachable callers omit an optional prop consumed inside its component
issue_types.label: Absent Optional Component Props
issue_types.note: Opt-in manual review candidate; defaults to off. Inspect caller evidence and defaults before changing the component. No automatic fix.

explanation.name: Absent optional component props
explanation.summary: Known reachable callers do not supply this used optional input; review defaults and API intent manually.
explanation.rationale: No caller passes the prop, so the code that reads it always runs with the default value. The other branch has no caller to test it, and the component looks more configurable than it is.
explanation.example: Card declares highlight?: boolean with a false default, reads highlight in its render body, and every inspected reachable caller renders <Card /> without highlight.
explanation.how_to_fix: Review inspected callers, defaults and API intent. Keep intentional stable props, update the component manually, or add a declaration-line fallow-ignore-next-line absent-component-prop comment. This candidate has no automatic fix.

issue_types.description: Each visible call passes a function parameter in the same way
issue_types.label: Constant Parameters
issue_types.note: Opt-in manual review candidate; defaults to off. Inspect the calls and the intent of the parameter before changing the function. No automatic fix.

explanation.name: Constant parameters
explanation.summary: Each visible call passes this parameter in one way; review the parameter and its callers manually.
explanation.rationale: A parameter of a module-scope function gets the same literal at each visible call (reason identical-argument), or an optional parameter is passed by no call (reason never-passed). The finding lists the value, the call count, the calls, and the count of conditions that test the parameter; a condition that tests a constant points at a branch that cannot run. Enable constant-parameters explicitly; it defaults to off. The rule fires only when each caller is visible. It abstains for public API and entry-point exports, exports that a plugin marks as used, dynamic imports, CommonJS, escaped namespaces, a function used as a value or through call/apply/bind, template hosts that can import the function, direct eval, classic scripts, framework auto-imports, open contracts (arguments, overloads, a reassigned binding, decorators, generators), a module with a parse error that can import the function, and fewer than 2 calls. A self-call that passes an optional parameter on blocks never-passed. A written, rest or destructured parameter gives no finding. In the default mode a test file is a caller; with --production only production callers count. Review the parameter manually; static analysis does not prove that no caller outside the project exists.
explanation.example: format(value, compact, locale?) is called 14 times in the project, each time as format(n, true). compact is always true, so the branch for false cannot run, and no call passes locale.
explanation.how_to_fix: Review the calls and the intent of the parameter. Remove the parameter and move the value into the function, or keep it when the flexibility is deliberate. Add a fallow-ignore-next-line constant-parameter comment above the parameter or the function to keep it. This candidate has no automatic fix.

issue_types.description: A Vue, Svelte, or React component prop is referenced nowhere in its own component
issue_types.label: Unused Component Props

explanation.name: Unused component props
explanation.summary: A Vue, Svelte, or React component prop is referenced nowhere in its own component
explanation.rationale: Callers pass a value that the component ignores, so a caller can think that the prop changes the output. The prop also stays in the component type and in every call site.
explanation.example: Widget.vue declares defineProps<{ size: string }>(), or a React Widget({ size }) destructures `size`, but `size` is referenced nowhere in the component (Vue: its script or template; React: its function body or JSX).
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the unused prop, or reference it in the component (Vue: the script / template; React: the function body or JSX). If the prop is part of a deliberately-stable public component API, suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line unused-component-prop.

issue_types.description: A Vue <script setup> defineEmits event is emitted nowhere in its own component
issue_types.label: Unused Component Emits

explanation.name: Unused component emits
explanation.summary: A Vue <script setup> defineEmits event is emitted nowhere in its own component
explanation.rationale: A parent can listen for an event that the component never emits. The handler of the parent never runs, and no error tells anyone.
explanation.example: Widget.vue declares defineEmits<{ close: [] }>() but `emit('close')` is called nowhere in the component's script.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the unused emit, or emit it in the script. If the emit is part of a deliberately-stable public component API, suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line unused-component-emit.

issue_types.description: An Angular @Input() / signal input() / model() input is read nowhere in its own component
issue_types.label: Unused Component Inputs

explanation.name: Unused component inputs
explanation.summary: An Angular @Input() / signal input() / model() input is read nowhere in its own component
explanation.rationale: An Angular `@Input()` / signal `input()` / `model()` declared input that is read nowhere in its own component (neither the inline / external template nor the class body). The Angular compiler never flags a declared-but-unread `@Input`, and there is no `@angular-eslint` rule for it. Conservative: usage detection over-credits by design (a template sentinel ref, any class-body member access by that name, or a bare identifier read counts as used), and the whole component abstains on an unresolved `extends` heritage clause (a base class in another file may read the input). A `model()` is recorded as an input only. Default warn; suppress or remove the input. The check runs only when the project declares `@angular/core`.
explanation.example: user-card.component.ts declares @Input() size: string (or size = input<string>()) but `size` is read nowhere in the template or the class body.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the unused input, or read it in the template or class body. If the input is part of a deliberately-stable public component API, suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line unused-component-input.

issue_types.description: An Angular @Output() / signal output() output is emitted nowhere in its own component
issue_types.label: Unused Component Outputs

explanation.name: Unused component outputs
explanation.summary: An Angular @Output() / signal output() output is emitted nowhere in its own component
explanation.rationale: A parent can bind to an output that the component never emits. The handler of the parent never runs, and no error tells anyone.
explanation.example: user-card.component.ts declares @Output() close = new EventEmitter<void>() (or close = output<void>()) but `this.close.emit(...)` is called nowhere in the class.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the unused output, or emit it from the class. If the output is part of a deliberately-stable public component API, suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line unused-component-output.

issue_types.description: A Svelte component dispatches a createEventDispatcher event whose name is listened to nowhere in the project
issue_types.label: Unused Svelte Events

explanation.name: Unused Svelte events
explanation.summary: A Svelte component dispatches a createEventDispatcher event whose name is listened to nowhere in the project
explanation.rationale: The component dispatches an event that no parent handles, so the action that the event reports has no effect. Readers assume that some parent reacts to it.
explanation.example: Child.svelte calls const dispatch = createEventDispatcher(); dispatch('dead'), but no parent listens for it (no <Child on:dead> anywhere in the project).
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the dispatched event, or listen for it on the component (<Child on:dead={...}> or forward it via <Child on:dead>). If the event is dispatched reflectively (a dynamic name) or is part of a deliberately-stable public component API, suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line unused-svelte-event.

issue_types.description: An Effect layer is composed only into layers that nothing uses
issue_types.label: Unused Effect Layers

explanation.name: Unused Effect layers
explanation.summary: An Effect layer is composed only into layers that nothing uses
explanation.rationale: An Effect `Layer` definition (a module-scope const or a class static property such as `static layer = Layer.effect(this, make)`) whose every reference sits inside other layer definitions that are themselves unused. The layer never reaches `Effect.provide`, `ManagedRuntime.make`, `Layer.launch` or any other runtime use. fallow builds a layer graph from `Layer.*` initializers and `.pipe(Layer.*)` chains. Any value reference outside a layer definition is a root, including references in functions and tests. A layer with zero references is not reported here: `unused-export` or `unused-class-member` reports it, so the rule reports the tail of a dead composition and names the unused consumers. Default warn. The check runs only when the project declares `effect`.
explanation.example: services.ts defines const CacheLive = Cache.layer.pipe(Layer.provide(Db.layer)) and export const OrphanLive = Layer.mergeAll(CacheLive), but nothing provides OrphanLive.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the unused consumer layers first, then this layer, or compose the layer into a layer that reaches a runtime. If code outside the analyzed project composes it, suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line unused-effect-layer.

issue_types.description: An Effect tagged error class is referenced only as a type or a catchTag string, and no code constructs or fails with it
issue_types.label: Unused Tagged Errors

explanation.name: Unused tagged errors
explanation.summary: An Effect tagged error class is referenced only as a type or a catchTag string, and no code constructs or fails with it
explanation.rationale: Types and `catchTag` handlers plan for a failure that no code produces. The handlers are dead code, and readers think that the failure can occur.
explanation.example: errors.ts declares class Expired extends Data.TaggedError("Expired"), signatures list it in the error channel and a handler calls catchTag("Expired"), but no code constructs Expired or fails with it.
explanation.how_to_fix: Fail with the error where the condition occurs, or remove the class, its type references and its catchTag handlers. If consumers outside the project construct or decode it, suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line unused-tagged-error.

issue_types.description: A catchTag handler names a project error tag that no code produces
issue_types.label: Unproduced Catch Tags

explanation.name: Unproduced catch tags
explanation.summary: A catchTag handler names a project error tag that no code produces
explanation.rationale: A `catchTag("X", ...)` or `catchTags({ X: ... })` handler where every project class with tag `X` is never constructed or failed with, and no object literal `_tag: "X"` or tagged constructor produces the tag. A tag that no project class declares can come from a package, so the rule abstains. Effect built-in tags such as `TimeoutException` are never reported. The rule reports a handler only when no `unused-tagged-error` finding covers its classes: the error rule is off, or its finding is suppressed. Default warn. The check runs only when the project declares `effect`.
explanation.example: main.ts calls Effect.catchTag("Expired", ...), the only class with tag Expired is never constructed, and the unused-tagged-error finding for it is suppressed.
explanation.how_to_fix: Remove the handler, or fail with the error where the condition occurs. If a package or code outside the project produces the tag, suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line unproduced-catch-tag.

issue_types.description: A Next.js Server Action exported from a "use server" file is referenced by no code in the project
issue_types.label: Unused Server Actions

explanation.name: Unused server actions
explanation.summary: A Next.js Server Action exported from a "use server" file is referenced by no code in the project
explanation.rationale: A Next.js Server Action (an export of a `"use server"` file) that no code in the project references: no import-and-call, no `action={fn}` JSX binding, no `<form action={fn}>`. This is the cross-graph "declared but zero consumers" direction, reclassified out of `unused-export` for `"use server"` files so the finding carries the action-specific signal. eslint-plugin-next is single-file and cannot see cross-file usage. It does not mean the endpoint is unreachable: Next.js still registers a generated action id, so it stays POST-able; it means no project code references it (likely forgotten or dead, and a candidate for removal to shrink surface area). Default warn; wire the action to a consumer or remove it. The check runs only when the project declares `next`.
explanation.example: app/actions.ts has "use server" and exports submitForm, but no component imports it, binds it via action={submitForm}, or uses it in <form action={submitForm}>.
explanation.how_to_fix: Wire the action to a consumer (an import-and-call, an action={fn} binding, or a <form action={fn}>), or remove it. If it is invoked reflectively (an action registry dispatching by id, or a non-JS caller), suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line unused-server-action.

issue_types.description: A SvelteKit load() return-object key is read by no consumer
issue_types.label: Unused Load Data Keys

explanation.name: Unused load data keys
explanation.summary: A SvelteKit load() return-object key is read by no consumer
explanation.rationale: A SvelteKit route `load()` (in `+page.ts` / `+page.server.ts` and the `.js` variants) returns an object whose keys become the route's `data` prop. A returned key that NO consumer reads is dead: it runs a real server-side fetch / DB cost on every request for data nothing renders. fallow checks two channels: the sibling `+page.svelte`'s `data.<key>` reads (route-pinned), and project-wide `page.data.<key>` (Svelte 5 `$app/state`) / `$page.data.<key>` (Svelte 4 `$app/stores`) reads in any component. `svelte-check` types `data` via generated `$types` but never flags an unread returned key. The detector abstains (never false-flags) on a spread / non-literal / multi-return / computed-key / wrapped `load`, on a sibling that passes the whole `data` object opaquely, on a `+page.server.ts` whose universal `+page.ts` sibling forwards its `data`, and project-wide when any whole-object use of `page.data` / `$page.data` is seen. Default warn; delete the key or wire a consumer. A load fetch can have side effects, so there is no safe auto-fix. The check runs only when the project declares `@sveltejs/kit`.
explanation.example: src/routes/blog/+page.ts returns { posts, draftCount } but +page.svelte only reads data.posts and no component reads page.data.draftCount.
explanation.how_to_fix: Delete the unused key from the load() return (and skip its fetch), or wire a consumer (read data.<key> in +page.svelte, or page.data.<key> in a shared component). If the load fetch has a side effect you must keep, suppress the line with // fallow-ignore-next-line unused-load-data-key.

issue_types.description: A React/Preact prop is forwarded unchanged through 2 or more components to a distant consumer
issue_types.label: Prop Drilling
issue_types.note: Opt-in: error gates CI; warn remains advisory even with --fail-on-issues. Defaults to off. Source-hop overrides decide severity.

explanation.name: Prop drilling
explanation.summary: A React/Preact prop is forwarded unchanged through 2 or more components to a distant consumer
explanation.rationale: A React/Preact prop is received by a component and forwarded unchanged to a child, which forwards it unchanged again, until a component uses it. One intermediate "pass-through" component is enough: the prop then passes unchanged through two components before the consumer. The high-confidence signal is that the received identifier appears only as the root of forwarded child-JSX attribute values (so `<Child userName={user.name}/>` counts: the prop `user` is projected forward), not the attribute name matching. fallow emits located per-chain records (the source, each pass-through hop, and the consumer with file + line + component name) so CI and an agent can act: colocate the consumer with the data, lift the value to a React context/provider at a mid-chain hop, or compose the component so the intermediates no longer thread the prop. This is a graph-derived health signal, not a correctness error. The rule defaults to off (opt-in), like private-type-leak and the security rules: enable it with `prop-drilling: "warn"` in `rules`. Set `prop-drilling: "error"` to enforce remaining chains in CI. Warnings remain advisory even with strict flags. File overrides resolve at the source hop and can activate the rule when the base setting is off. Suppressed or baselined chains do not gate. Zero false positives by construction: any `{...props}` spread, `cloneElement`, element-as-prop / render-prop / children-as-function, or context `*.Provider` anywhere in the chain abstains the whole chain, as does an ambiguous or unresolvable hop. The check runs only when the project declares `react` / `react-dom` / `next` / `preact`.
explanation.example: Page receives `user` and renders <Layout user={user}/>; Layout only re-passes it to <Sidebar user={user}/>; Sidebar only re-passes it to <Profile user={user}/>, which finally reads user.name. The prop is drilled through Layout and Sidebar untouched.
explanation.how_to_fix: Collapse the chain: colocate the consumer with the data, lift the value into a React context/provider at a mid-chain hop and consume it there, or compose the component (pass the rendered child as children) so the intermediates no longer thread the prop. Enable the rule with rules.prop-drilling = "warn" (it defaults to off). To accept one chain, suppress the source prop with // fallow-ignore-next-line prop-drilling.

issue_types.description: A React/Preact component whose whole body is a single spread-forwarded child render (a candidate for inlining)
issue_types.label: Thin Wrappers
issue_types.note: Opt-in: set rules.thin-wrapper to warn or error to enable. Defaults to off.

explanation.name: Thin wrapper
explanation.summary: A React/Preact component whose whole body is a single spread-forwarded child render (a candidate for inlining)
explanation.rationale: A React/Preact component whose entire body is structural indirection: it returns exactly one capitalized component element that forwards the component's own props via a bare spread (`return <Child {...props}/>`), with no host-element wrapper, no extra children, no named attributes alongside the spread, no hooks, no branching, and no other statements. Such a component adds nothing of its own: it is a candidate for inlining at its call sites or deleting, not a correctness error. fallow emits a located per-wrapper record (file + line + the wrapper and child component names) so CI and an agent can act. The rule defaults to off (opt-in), like prop-drilling and the security rules: enable it with `thin-wrapper: "warn"` in `rules`. Zero false positives by construction: a `forwardRef` / `memo` wrapper (the sanctioned way to make a child ref-able or set a perf boundary), an exported component (a public-API re-brand / encapsulation), a context `*.Provider` wrapper, a `cloneElement` / render-prop forward, a wrapper that passes any named attribute alongside the spread (a fixed configuration), a self-render, or an unresolvable / member-expression child all abstain. A TypeScript-only type-narrowing wrapper (`const StrictButton = (p: StrictProps) => <Button {...p}/>`) is a known limitation, because fallow reads syntax and does not resolve types; suppress it with the inline comment. The check runs only when the project declares `react` / `react-dom` / `next` / `preact`.
explanation.example: const ButtonWrapper = (props) => <Button {...props}/>; the wrapper has no own markup, hooks, or logic, so it only re-points at Button.
explanation.how_to_fix: Inline the wrapper at its call sites (use <Button .../> directly) or delete it. Keep it only if it is a deliberate seam (a planned divergence point, a public-API re-brand): an exported wrapper already abstains. Enable the rule with rules.thin-wrapper = "warn" (it defaults to off). To accept one wrapper, suppress it with // fallow-ignore-next-line thin-wrapper above the component definition.

issue_types.description: Three or more React/Preact components across two or more files declare an identical prop-name set (a missing shared Props type)
issue_types.label: Duplicate Prop Shapes
issue_types.note: Opt-in: set rules.duplicate-prop-shape to warn or error to enable. Defaults to off.

explanation.name: Duplicate prop shape
explanation.summary: Three or more React/Preact components across two or more files declare an identical prop-name set (a missing shared Props type)
explanation.rationale: Three or more distinct React/Preact components, living in two or more files, whose statically-harvested prop name set is byte-for-byte identical after (a) excluding a fixed denylist of ubiquitous DOM / render-passthrough prop names (className, style, id, children, key, ref, the common event handlers, plus data-* / aria-* by prefix) and (b) requiring the remaining significant set to have four or more members. Identity is over names only, never types (fallow does not resolve types). This is a structural-refactor health signal: the recurring shape is a missing shared abstraction, so extract one shared `Props` type (or a base component) that every member reuses. It is never a correctness error and never an auto-fix. fallow emits one located record per participating component, each naming the shared `shape`, the `group_size`, and the other members in `sharing_components`.
