The rule defaults to off (opt-in), like thin-wrapper and the security rules: enable it with `duplicate-prop-shape: "warn"` in `rules`. Anti-noise gates (defended as rule-of-three plus a denylist-survivor floor, not tuned magic): the four-significant-prop floor turns `{label, onClick}` buttons into non-findings; the three-component floor is the rule-of-three abstraction trigger; the two-file floor keeps a local same-shaped variant pair (a render-prop pair, a Foo/FooImpl split) unflagged. A component whose props are not fully harvestable (a rest/spread signature, a forwardRef/memo over an imported interface) abstains, because a partial prop set can never be proven identical. Exact full-set identity only: a superset / subset relationship does not group, so a four-prop group and a five-prop superset form two findings (the price of zero invalid groups: the finding always fits one extracted shared type). The check runs only when the project declares `react` / `react-dom` / `next` / `preact`.
explanation.example: FieldText, FieldNumber, and FieldSelect (across three files) each declare exactly { name, label, value, onChange, error }. The five significant prop names are identical, so they form one duplicate-prop-shape group.
explanation.how_to_fix: Extract one shared Props type (e.g. type FieldProps = { name; label; value; onChange; error }) that every member reuses, or a base component the variants compose. Keep them separate only if a per-variant prop divergence is planned. Enable the rule with rules.duplicate-prop-shape = "warn" (it defaults to off). To accept one member, suppress it with // fallow-ignore-next-line duplicate-prop-shape above the component definition; the suppressed member still appears in its siblings' sharing_components because the group is real regardless of suppression.

issue_types.description: Two or more Next.js App Router route files resolve to the same URL
issue_types.label: Route Collisions

explanation.name: Route collision
explanation.summary: Two or more Next.js App Router route files resolve to the same URL
explanation.rationale: Two or more App Router route files (a `page` or a `route` handler) resolve to the same URL within one app-root. Route groups `(name)` and parallel slots `@name` do not change the URL, so `app/(marketing)/about/page.tsx` and `app/(shop)/about/page.tsx` both own `/about`. Next.js fails the build ("You cannot have two parallel pages that resolve to the same path") because a URL can have at most one owner, whether a Page or a Route Handler. fallow surfaces every colliding file at once; the build error names only one. Buckets are scoped per app-root (per workspace package), so a monorepo with several independent Next apps sharing a path is not flagged. Files under a private `_folder` or an intercepting marker `(.)`/`(..)`/`(...)` are excluded. There is no safe auto-fix: move or merge one of the files so each URL has a single owner. The check runs only when the project declares `next`.
explanation.example: `app/(marketing)/about/page.tsx` and `app/(shop)/about/page.tsx` both resolve to the URL `/about`.
explanation.how_to_fix: Move or merge one of the files, so that each URL has one page or one route handler.

issue_types.description: Sibling Next.js dynamic route segments use different slug names at the same position
issue_types.label: Dynamic Segment Conflicts

explanation.name: Dynamic segment name conflict
explanation.summary: Sibling Next.js dynamic route segments use different slug names at the same position
explanation.rationale: Two or more sibling dynamic route segments at the same App Router tree position use different param spellings (`[id]` vs `[slug]`, or a catch-all `[...x]` vs an optional catch-all `[[...x]]`). Next.js throws "You cannot use different slug names for the same dynamic path" at dev and production runtime when the position is hit, because one position must resolve to a single param name. `next build` does not catch this (the build succeeds), so CI passes while the route crashes on its first request; fallow's static catch closes that gap. Route groups are transparent to the position and parallel slots fork it, so only genuinely-sibling segments conflict. To fix: rename the dynamic segments at the position to one consistent slug name. The check runs only when the project declares `next`.
explanation.example: `app/blog/[id]/page.tsx` and `app/blog/[slug]/edit/page.tsx` use two names for the dynamic segment at the same position.
explanation.how_to_fix: Rename the dynamic segments at that position to one name, for example `[slug]` in both paths.

issue_types.description: Function has high cyclomatic complexity

explanation.name: High Cyclomatic Complexity
explanation.summary: Function has high cyclomatic complexity
explanation.rationale: McCabe cyclomatic complexity exceeds the configured threshold. Cyclomatic complexity counts the number of independent paths through a function (1 + decision points: if/else, switch cases, loops, ternary, logical operators). High values indicate functions that are hard to test exhaustively. fallow also emits this rule on synthetic `<template>` findings across every supported template dialect (Angular .html templates and inline `@Component({ template: ... })` literals, Vue SFC `<template>` blocks, Svelte markup, Astro markup), counting each dialect's control-flow blocks (Angular `@if`/`@else if`/`@for`/`@case`/`@defer (when ...)` and legacy `*ngIf`/`*ngFor`; Vue `v-if`/`v-else-if`/`v-for`; Svelte `{#if}`/`{:else if}`/`{#each}`/`{#await}`/`{#key}`; the Astro equivalents) plus ternary and logical operators inside bound attributes and interpolations; on each top-level Svelte `{#snippet name(...)}` block, emitted as its own `<snippet:NAME>` unit; and on synthetic `<component>` rollup findings whose `cyclomatic` is the worst class method's score plus the template's. Ranking and `--targets` use the rollup total; JSON exposes the per-half breakdown under `component_rollup`.
explanation.example: `function route(req)` has a `switch` with 14 `case` labels and two `if` checks. Its cyclomatic complexity is 17, while `health.maxCyclomatic` is 15.
explanation.how_to_fix: For function findings, extract named helpers, split independent branches, flatten guard clauses, and add tests around the behavior before refactoring. For `<template>` findings, flatten nested control flow and move branch selection out of the markup: Angular `@if`/`@for`/`@switch`/`@defer` and legacy `*ngIf`/`*ngFor` into computed signals on the component class, Vue `v-if`/`v-else-if`/`v-for` into computed properties, Svelte `{#if}`/`{:else if}`/`{#each}`/`{#await}`/`{#key}` into derived state, Astro control flow into props resolved in the frontmatter. In Svelte, moving a repeated or deeply nested block into a top-level `{#snippet}` gives it its own `<snippet:NAME>` unit with nesting rebased to zero, so the in-file extraction moves the score; splitting a large template into child components lowers the score in every dialect. For `<component>` rollup findings, attack the larger half first; the per-half breakdown lives in `component_rollup`. To report these findings without a failed run, set the `complexity-cyclomatic` or `complexity-cognitive` rule to `warn`.

issue_types.description: Function has high cognitive complexity

explanation.name: High Cognitive Complexity
explanation.summary: Function has high cognitive complexity
explanation.rationale: SonarSource cognitive complexity exceeds the configured threshold. Unlike cyclomatic complexity, cognitive complexity penalizes nesting depth and non-linear control flow (breaks, continues, early returns). It measures how hard a function is to understand when reading sequentially. fallow also emits this rule on synthetic `<template>` findings across every supported template dialect (Angular .html templates and inline `@Component({ template: ... })` literals, Vue SFC `<template>` blocks, Svelte markup, Astro markup), where nesting penalties accumulate on stacked control-flow blocks: Angular `@if`/`@for`/`@switch`, Vue `v-if`/`v-for`, Svelte `{#if}`/`{#each}`/`{#await}`; on each top-level Svelte `{#snippet name(...)}` block, emitted as its own `<snippet:NAME>` unit with nesting rebased to zero so in-file snippet extraction lowers the parent template's score; and on synthetic `<component>` rollup findings whose `cognitive` is the worst class method's score plus the template's. Ranking and `--targets` use the rollup total; JSON exposes the per-half breakdown under `component_rollup`.
explanation.example: `applyDiscount` puts an `if` inside a `for` inside another `if`, with a `continue` and a `&&` chain in the inner block. Each nesting level adds to the score, which reaches 21 while `health.maxCognitive` is 15.
explanation.how_to_fix: For function findings, extract named helpers, split independent branches, flatten guard clauses, and add tests around the behavior before refactoring. For `<template>` findings, flatten nested control flow and move branch selection out of the markup: Angular `@if`/`@for`/`@switch`/`@defer` and legacy `*ngIf`/`*ngFor` into computed signals on the component class, Vue `v-if`/`v-else-if`/`v-for` into computed properties, Svelte `{#if}`/`{:else if}`/`{#each}`/`{#await}`/`{#key}` into derived state, Astro control flow into props resolved in the frontmatter. In Svelte, moving a repeated or deeply nested block into a top-level `{#snippet}` gives it its own `<snippet:NAME>` unit with nesting rebased to zero, so the in-file extraction moves the score; splitting a large template into child components lowers the score in every dialect. For `<component>` rollup findings, attack the larger half first; the per-half breakdown lives in `component_rollup`. To report these findings without a failed run, set the `complexity-cyclomatic` or `complexity-cognitive` rule to `warn`.

issue_types.description: Function exceeds both complexity thresholds

explanation.name: High Complexity (Both)
explanation.summary: Function exceeds both complexity thresholds
explanation.rationale: Function exceeds both cyclomatic and cognitive complexity thresholds. This is the strongest signal that a function needs refactoring, it has many paths and is hard to understand. The same rule fires on synthetic `<template>` findings in every supported template dialect (Angular .html templates and inline `@Component({ template: ... })` literals, Vue SFC `<template>` blocks, Svelte markup, Astro markup) when both metrics exceed their thresholds, and on synthetic `<component>` rollup findings whose totals are the worst class method's score plus the template's. Ranking and `--targets` use the rollup totals; JSON exposes the per-half breakdown under `component_rollup`.
explanation.example: `parseRow` has a cyclomatic complexity of 24 and a cognitive complexity of 31, so the function exceeds both thresholds: it has many paths, and the paths are deeply nested.
explanation.how_to_fix: For function findings, extract named helpers, split independent branches, flatten guard clauses, and add tests around the behavior before refactoring. For `<template>` findings, flatten nested control flow and move branch selection out of the markup: Angular `@if`/`@for`/`@switch`/`@defer` and legacy `*ngIf`/`*ngFor` into computed signals on the component class, Vue `v-if`/`v-else-if`/`v-for` into computed properties, Svelte `{#if}`/`{:else if}`/`{#each}`/`{#await}`/`{#key}` into derived state, Astro control flow into props resolved in the frontmatter. In Svelte, moving a repeated or deeply nested block into a top-level `{#snippet}` gives it its own `<snippet:NAME>` unit with nesting rebased to zero, so the in-file extraction moves the score; splitting a large template into child components lowers the score in every dialect. For `<component>` rollup findings, attack the larger half first; the per-half breakdown lives in `component_rollup`. To report these findings without a failed run, set the `complexity-cyclomatic` or `complexity-cognitive` rule to `warn`.

issue_types.description: Function has a high CRAP score (complexity combined with low coverage)

explanation.name: High CRAP Score
explanation.summary: Function has a high CRAP score (complexity combined with low coverage)
explanation.rationale: The function's CRAP (Change Risk Anti-Patterns) score meets or exceeds the configured threshold. CRAP combines cyclomatic complexity with test coverage using the Savoia and Evans (2007) formula: `CC^2 * (1 - coverage/100)^3 + CC`. High CRAP indicates changes to this function carry high risk because it is complex and poorly tested. Pair with `--coverage` for accurate per-function scoring; without it fallow estimates coverage from the module graph. This rule fires on functions only: synthetic template-family units (`<template>`, Svelte `<snippet:NAME>`) are excluded from the CRAP dimension, because a template is exercised only through its component and carries no coverage the formula could measure. Templates gate on the cyclomatic and cognitive dimensions instead.
explanation.example: A complex function has little or no matching Istanbul coverage, so its CRAP score crosses the configured gate. Synthetic template-family units (the `<template>` units on Angular, Vue, Svelte and Astro markup, and Svelte `<snippet:NAME>` units) are not scored on this dimension: a template carries no direct coverage of its own, so fallow gates templates on the cyclomatic and cognitive dimensions instead.
explanation.how_to_fix: Add focused tests for the risky branches first, then simplify the function if the score remains high. Template findings never carry this rule, so a `maxCrap` override scoped to a template unit buys nothing and can be removed. To report these findings without a failed run, set the `complexity-crap` rule to `warn`.

issue_types.description: File has more lines than the file-length threshold

explanation.name: Long File
explanation.summary: File has more lines than the file-length threshold
explanation.rationale: A long file is slow to review and to search. More changes touch the same file, so merge conflicts happen more often.
explanation.example: A module grew to 900 physical lines while `health.maxFileLines` is 500. Blank lines and comment lines count; a final newline does not add a line.
explanation.how_to_fix: Move cohesive groups of exports into their own modules, and remove unused code. In `fallow audit`, a long file that did not grow stays inherited, so you can enable the threshold on an existing project and stop further growth. To report these findings without a failed run, set the `complexity-file-lines` rule to `warn`. To raise the ceiling for generated files, use `thresholdOverrides[].maxFileLines`.

issue_types.description: File identified as a high-priority refactoring candidate

explanation.name: Refactoring Target
explanation.summary: File identified as a high-priority refactoring candidate
explanation.rationale: File identified as a refactoring candidate based on a weighted combination of complexity density, churn velocity, dead code ratio, fan-in (blast radius), and fan-out (coupling). Categories: urgent churn+complexity, break circular dependency, split high-impact file, remove dead code, extract complex functions, reduce coupling.
explanation.example: A file combines high complexity density, churn, fan-in, and dead-code signals.
explanation.how_to_fix: Start with the listed evidence: remove dead exports, extract complex functions, then reduce fan-out or cycles in small steps.

issue_types.description: CSS or CSS-in-JS hardcoded styling value bypasses the design token system
issue_types.label: CSS Token Drift

explanation.name: CSS Token Drift
explanation.summary: CSS or CSS-in-JS hardcoded styling value bypasses the design token system
explanation.rationale: A hardcoded value does not follow a change of the design token. A theme or brand update misses this place, and the interface becomes inconsistent.
explanation.example: Markup uses `class="w-[13px] bg-[#1a2b3c]"`, Tailwind arbitrary values, or a stylesheet sets `color: #1a2b3c` where the project has color tokens.
explanation.how_to_fix: Replace the value with the nearest token of the scale. Keep the value when the one-off value is deliberate.

issue_types.description: CSS or CSS-in-JS declaration block is duplicated across rules
issue_types.label: CSS Duplicate Block

explanation.name: CSS Duplicate Block
explanation.summary: CSS or CSS-in-JS declaration block is duplicated across rules
explanation.rationale: A style rule declaration block is repeated across selectors, suggesting copy-pasted styling that can often be consolidated. The finding is advisory by default and does not affect the audit verdict unless rules.css-duplicate-block is set to error.
explanation.example: `.card` in src/card.css and `.panel` in src/panel.css declare the same four or more declarations.
explanation.how_to_fix: Move the shared declarations to one class or a shared mixin, and use it from both places.

issue_types.description: CSS selector, nesting, or important usage is structurally complex
issue_types.label: CSS Selector Complexity

explanation.name: CSS Selector Complexity
explanation.summary: CSS selector, nesting, or important usage is structurally complex
explanation.rationale: A selector with high specificity or `!important` wins over later rules, so the next style change needs a stronger selector. A long descendant chain also breaks when the markup changes.
explanation.example: `.sidebar nav ul li a.active` sits four levels deep in nested SCSS, and its block uses `!important` on most declarations.
explanation.how_to_fix: Flatten the nesting, put a class on the element instead of a long descendant chain, and remove `!important` where the order of the rules can do the work.

issue_types.description: CSS or CSS-in-JS surface appears unused
issue_types.label: CSS Dead Surface

explanation.name: CSS Dead Surface
explanation.summary: CSS or CSS-in-JS surface appears unused
explanation.rationale: The unused style still ships to users and still gets updated in redesigns. A dead scoped class often means that the markup changed and the style stayed behind.
explanation.example: Card.vue defines `.card__badge` in `<style scoped>`, but no part of the component uses that class.
explanation.how_to_fix: Delete the unused class after you check that no code adds it at runtime, for example through a class name built from a variable.

issue_types.description: CSS or CSS-in-JS reference resolves to no stylesheet definition
issue_types.label: CSS Broken Reference

explanation.name: CSS Broken Reference
explanation.summary: CSS or CSS-in-JS reference resolves to no stylesheet definition
explanation.rationale: The class or animation name has no definition, so the element gets no style or no animation. The browser reports no error, so the defect shows only on screen.
explanation.example: src/app.css sets `animation: fade-in 1s`, but no stylesheet defines `@keyframes fade-in`. Or markup uses `class="nav-item"` where only `.nav-items` exists.
explanation.how_to_fix: Correct the name or add the missing definition. Keep the reference when a CSS-in-JS library or an external stylesheet defines the name.

issue_types.description: Runtime-reachable file has no test dependency path

explanation.name: Untested File
explanation.summary: Runtime-reachable file has no test dependency path
explanation.rationale: No test imports the file, directly or through other modules. A change to the file can break production, and no test fails.
explanation.example: `src/routes/checkout.ts` imports `src/billing/invoice.ts`, but no test file imports either module, directly or through other modules.
explanation.how_to_fix: Add or wire a test that imports the runtime path, or update entry-point/test discovery if the existing test is invisible to fallow.

issue_types.description: Runtime-reachable export has no test dependency path

explanation.name: Untested Export
explanation.summary: Runtime-reachable export has no test dependency path
explanation.rationale: No test reaches the export. A change to its behavior can break the production code that uses it, and no test fails.
explanation.example: `src/cart.ts` calls `roundCents` from `src/money.ts`. `test/money.test.ts` imports only `formatPrice` from that file, so no test reaches `roundCents`.
explanation.how_to_fix: Add or wire a test that imports the runtime path, or update entry-point/test discovery if the existing test is invisible to fallow.

issue_types.description: Statically unused and never invoked in production
issue_types.note: Requires --runtime-coverage input (V8 directory, V8 JSON, or Istanbul map)
issue_types.license_note: A single local runtime-coverage capture is free; continuous or multi-capture runtime monitoring requires an active license (fallow license activate).

explanation.name: Production Safe To Delete
explanation.summary: Statically unused and never invoked in production
explanation.rationale: The function is both statically unreachable in the module graph and was never invoked during the observed runtime coverage window. This is the highest-confidence delete signal fallow emits.
explanation.example: No module references `formatLegacyInvoice` in src/billing/legacy.ts, and the production capture shows no call to it.
explanation.how_to_fix: Check that the capture window covers rare paths, such as a monthly job, then delete the function.

issue_types.description: Statically used but never invoked in production
issue_types.note: Requires --runtime-coverage input (V8 directory, V8 JSON, or Istanbul map)
issue_types.license_note: A single local runtime-coverage capture is free; continuous or multi-capture runtime monitoring requires an active license (fallow license activate).

explanation.name: Production Review Required
explanation.summary: Statically used but never invoked in production
explanation.rationale: The function is reachable in the module graph (or exercised by tests / untracked call sites) but was not invoked during the observed runtime coverage window. Needs a human look: may be seasonal, error-path only, or legitimately unused.
explanation.example: src/reports/page.tsx imports `exportCsv`, but the production capture shows no call to it.
explanation.how_to_fix: Ask the owner whether the path is seasonal, an error path or dead. Remove the call sites and the function when nobody needs them.

issue_types.description: Function was invoked below the low-traffic threshold
issue_types.note: Requires --runtime-coverage input (V8 directory, V8 JSON, or Istanbul map)
issue_types.license_note: A single local runtime-coverage capture is free; continuous or multi-capture runtime monitoring requires an active license (fallow license activate).

explanation.name: Production Low Traffic
explanation.summary: Function was invoked below the low-traffic threshold
explanation.rationale: Production almost never runs the function, but the team still maintains and tests it. Each change to it carries risk for a path that few requests need.
explanation.example: `legacyLogin` ran 3 times in a capture of 2 million calls, below the `--low-traffic-threshold` fraction.
explanation.how_to_fix: Find the remaining callers, move them to the current path, then remove the function. Keep it when the rare callers matter.

issue_types.description: Runtime coverage could not be resolved for this function
issue_types.note: Requires --runtime-coverage input (V8 directory, V8 JSON, or Istanbul map)
issue_types.license_note: A single local runtime-coverage capture is free; continuous or multi-capture runtime monitoring requires an active license (fallow license activate).

explanation.name: Runtime Coverage Unavailable
explanation.summary: Runtime coverage could not be resolved for this function
explanation.rationale: fallow has no runtime data for the function, so it cannot tell if production runs it. A decision to delete or keep the function has no runtime evidence.
explanation.example: `renderChart` runs in a worker thread, so the capture of the main process has no coverage entry for it.
explanation.how_to_fix: Capture coverage in the worker too, or check that the source maps map the bundle to the source file. Do not delete code because of this finding.

issue_types.description: Runtime coverage gave no verdict for this function
issue_types.note: Requires --runtime-coverage input (V8 directory, V8 JSON, or Istanbul map)
issue_types.license_note: A single local runtime-coverage capture is free; continuous or multi-capture runtime monitoring requires an active license (fallow license activate).

explanation.name: Runtime Coverage
explanation.summary: Runtime coverage gave no verdict for this function
explanation.rationale: The runtime data gave no known verdict for the function. A decision to delete or keep the function has no runtime evidence until fallow can read the verdict.

issue_types.description: Syntactic security sink candidates require verification

explanation.name: Tainted Sink Candidates
explanation.summary: Syntactic security sink candidates require verification
explanation.rationale: The `tainted-sink` family covers data-driven `fallow security` catalogue categories. These findings are unverified candidates, not confirmed vulnerabilities. fallow can connect known source signals to captured sink shapes and add CWE metadata, but it does not prove attacker control, missing sanitization, exploitability, or business impact.

explanation.example: A module marked `use client` imports code that reads a non-public `process.env` or `import.meta.env` value through a static path.
explanation.how_to_fix: Keep non-public env reads on the server side, move the value behind an API boundary, or rename only intentionally public values to the framework's public prefix.

issue_types.description: The change weakens tests or a coverage threshold
issue_types.label: Weakened Tests

explanation.name: Weakened Tests
explanation.summary: The change weakens tests or a coverage threshold
explanation.rationale: `fallow audit` compares the base and head text of each changed file. The `kind` field tells how the change weakened the tests: `skip-only` (a new `.skip`, `.only`, `xit` or `fit` marker), `removed-tests` (fewer test cases in a file, while the total of all changed test files also dropped), `assertion-drop` (fewer `expect`, `assert` or `should` calls in a test file with no test case removed), `coverage-threshold` (a coverage or quality threshold that is less strict), `rule-severity` (a rule severity in the Fallow config that is less strict, such as `error` to `off`, a removed rule whose default is weaker, or a new `overrides` entry that turns a rule off for some paths), or `ignore-pattern` (a new or broader entry in a config key that removes files or findings from the analysis or makes code count as used, or a removed `!` exception of `ignorePatterns` or `ignoreFindings`). The keys are `ignorePatterns`, `ignoreFindings`, `production.ignore`, `health.ignore`, `duplicates.ignore`, `duplicates.ignoredClones`, `entry`, `supportEntry`, `dynamicallyLoaded`, `publicPackages`, `usedClassMembers`, `ignoreDependencies`, `ignoreBinaries`, `ignoreUnresolvedImports`, `ignoreExports`, `ignoreCatalogReferences`, `ignoreDependencyOverrides` and `boundaries.coverage.allowUnmatched`. The evidence names the key. A new entry that a base entry or a built-in default already covers does not report. The config check follows each relative `extends` file, so a change in an extended file or in the `extends` list reports too. A value that an `npm:` package or an `https://` URL can set does not compare, because the audit cannot read it at the base. A `rule-severity` or `ignore-pattern` finding takes the stricter of the base and head `weakened-tests` severity, so a change that turns off `weakened-tests` still reports. A suppression comment in the head config does not hide it, and it has no suppression action. A drop does not report when the lost test lines name code that the change removed, such as a deleted function or a deleted fixture directory: the tests went with that code. A name of a deleted file that a changed file still holds, a name that a deleted file only imports, a directory that still exists, and a reserved word such as `import` do not count. An assertion drop reports only when assertions are at least half of the code lines that the file lost, so a test rewrite that moves setup checks into a helper does not report. The finding is a fact about the change, not a proof that coverage dropped. Defaults to `warn`.
explanation.example: A change turns `it('charges tax', ...)` into `it.skip('charges tax', ...)`, or lowers `coverage.thresholds.lines` from 90 to 70.
explanation.how_to_fix: Decide if the weaker test or threshold is intended. If it is, suppress the finding with `// fallow-ignore-next-line weakened-tests` (or `fallow-ignore-file` for a file-level kind), or set the rule to `off` for the path in `overrides`.

issue_types.description: The change adds a suppression comment
issue_types.label: Added Suppressions

explanation.name: Added Suppressions
explanation.summary: The change adds a suppression comment
explanation.rationale: `fallow audit` reports a comment line that the change adds with a lint, type-check, coverage or Fallow suppression: `eslint-disable`, `oxlint-disable`, `biome-ignore`, `deno-lint-ignore`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `@ts-nocheck`, `istanbul ignore`, `c8 ignore`, `v8 ignore` or `fallow-ignore`. A moved comment is not added. A `fallow-ignore` comment that names only diff-risk rules does not count. Files below a fixture or generated directory (`fixture`, `fixtures`, `__fixtures__`, `__snapshots__`, `generated`, `__generated__`) do not report, because a tool writes them or a test reads them as data. Defaults to `warn`.
explanation.example: A change adds `// @ts-expect-error` above a call instead of a correct type.
explanation.how_to_fix: Decide if the suppression is necessary. If it is, keep it and suppress the finding with `// fallow-ignore-next-line added-suppression`, or turn the rule off for the path.

issue_types.description: The change adds a test-environment branch to source code
issue_types.label: Test-Only Branches

explanation.name: Test-Only Branches
explanation.summary: The change adds a test-environment branch to source code
explanation.rationale: The tests run a path that production never runs. A passing test then does not prove that the production path works.
explanation.example: A change adds `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'test') return cached;` to `src/pricing.ts`.
explanation.how_to_fix: Prefer a seam that tests can inject, such as a parameter or a module mock. If the branch is intended, suppress it with `// fallow-ignore-next-line test-only-branch`.

issue_types.description: The change edits one copy of duplicated code but not its siblings
issue_types.label: Diverged Clone Siblings

explanation.name: Diverged Clone Siblings
explanation.summary: The change edits one copy of duplicated code but not its siblings
explanation.rationale: `fallow audit` reports a base clone group where the change edited exactly one copy, the edit broke the clone, and every other copy kept its text. The siblings can need the same change. A cosmetic edit that keeps the clone, a removed copy, a change that edits every copy, and an edit to a test or story copy do not report. Needs the base snapshot of `--gate new-only`. Opt-in: defaults to `off`, because copies often differ on purpose, for example an input and an output type, or a legacy copy. Set it to `warn` or `error` to review every diverged copy.
explanation.example: `src/a/total.ts` and `src/b/total.ts` held the same function. The change fixes a bug in the first copy only.
explanation.how_to_fix: Check the unchanged copies in `related`. Apply the same change there, or extract a shared function. If the copies must differ, suppress with `// fallow-ignore-next-line diverged-clone-sibling`.

issue_types.description: The change adds a dependency
issue_types.label: Added Dependencies

explanation.name: Added Dependencies
explanation.summary: The change adds a dependency
explanation.rationale: `fallow audit` reports a dependency that the change adds to a `package.json`. A new dependency is often correct, so the rule defaults to `off`. Set it to `warn` or `error` to review every new package. An invented package name already fails as an unresolved import or an unlisted dependency.
explanation.example: A change adds `"left-pad": "^1.3.0"` to `dependencies`.
explanation.how_to_fix: Check that the package exists, is maintained, and is not already covered by a dependency of the project. Suppress through `overrides` because `package.json` cannot hold a comment.

issue_types.description: A small code change made no test fail

explanation.name: Survived Mutants
explanation.summary: A small code change made no test fail
explanation.rationale: `fallow mutation` makes one small change to the code, such as `>=` to `>`, and runs the tests that reach the changed line. A survived mutant is a change that made no test fail, so the tests do not check that behavior. The CI integrations report a survived mutant on a changed line as a warning finding (CodeClimate severity `minor`). The finding names the operator, the function and the mutant id, and never the source text. A mutant that no test reaches (`no_coverage`) is not a finding. No `rules.*` key gates the finding: the mutation score gate (`--min-score` or `mutation.minScore`) decides the exit code.
explanation.example: The tests call `isAdult(30)` and `isAdult(10)` only. Changing `>=` to `>` in `isAdult` makes no test fail, because no test checks the age `18`.
explanation.how_to_fix: Add or change a test so that it fails on this change. To see the code, run `fallow mutation inspect` with the mutant ID that the finding names.
